items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: I met Snoozer when Peck Kelly sent for me... I recorded him... I had to play along, as you'll see pretty soon, with him.

ctx.x: over. We'll be back right after this. This is WTIS on the subject of New Orleans jazz, a subject we certainly should have presented before now, but I can assure you that we will do this again and again, especially since those phones are ringing like they are. The line, when they become available, available, 523-2404. The present time in downtown New Orleans, we have partly cloudy skies with a temperature of 60 WTIX degrees. items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: I was going to use Snoozer Quinn on guitar and Siegfried Christensen on piano and Eddie Miller on clarinet and I was going to play cornet... Well, we rehearsed and the trombone player couldn't learn it the first day... So that was the end of that.

ctx.x: I don't know what Celestine was doing. It was Schatz for a while. It was Schatz Madison.

I don't know, but one of them was a mean man and the other one was, one trumpet player was a mean guy and the other one was a very nice fellow. Well, I set them to rehearsing across, Wailines had a sort of a warehouse across the street and without getting any permission because I knew I couldn't get permission for this, I just took it upon myself to take them over there.
